A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 32-page versions of Heterogeneous Decentralized Diffusion Models. Their main text, equations, references, figures, tables, and appendices can be matched throughout.

before.justification: v2 reports original image-generation experiments in Section 4 and the supplement, including FID, CLIP, LPIPS, convergence measurements, and qualitative comparisons.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, including the homogeneous-versus-heterogeneous results in Table 4 and supplementary routing and sampling analyses.

M1.justification: The heterogeneous expert framework, prediction conversion, routing, AdaLN-Single architecture, and checkpoint initialization procedures are identical in Sections 3, 6, and 8.

E1.justification: LAION-Aesthetics and LAION-Art training and evaluation coverage is unchanged. The appendices retain the same text-to-image scenarios and prompts.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical across corresponding experiments, including monolithic, native DDPM/FM, converted-DDPM, combined-expert, and homogeneous configurations in Tables 1–4.

E3.justification: Reported model sizes, training budgets, preprocessing, metrics, and sample counts are unchanged. Both retain CFG 7.5 with 50 steps for aligned comparisons and CFG 6 with 75 steps for conversion analyses.

E4.justification: The initialization comparison and supplementary routing-threshold, expert-ordering, noise-schedule, and sampling-strategy analyses are unchanged, including Figures 3, 6, and 13–16.

E5.justification: Both retain identical uncertainty-reporting practices, including CLIP ± reporting in Table 3 and LPIPS ± reporting in Section 4.4. Seed-related descriptions and statistical information are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted findings, and generated examples match. For example, Table 4 retains FID 11.88 for 2DDPM:6FM and 12.45 for 8FM under the same aligned inference settings.

T1.justification: Proposition 1, its assumptions and proof in Section 3.3, and the conversion derivations in Sections 3.2 and 8.1 are identical. No mathematical definitions or reasoning change.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about heterogeneous fusion, checkpoint transfer, architectural efficiency, resource requirements, and generation quality and diversity.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are identical, including quality–diversity trade-offs, high-noise conversion instability, hand-tuned safeguards, and restricted objective and expert-ratio coverage.

D1.justification: Sections 6 and 8 retain identical preprocessing instructions, hyperparameters, hardware and training-time disclosures, initialization details, and numerical safeguards. Code and data access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the 40 references, and the positioning relative to DDM, diffusion parameterization, Flow Matching, and efficient architectures are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v2 dated 1 Jun 2026 to v3 dated 31 Jul 2026. All other extracted text, terminology, headings, and document organization are identical.

P2.justification: The first-page arXiv margin stamp moves rightward and downward. All figures, tables, captions, and body layouts remain unchanged; rendered pages 2–32 match exactly.

improvement.justification: v3 changes only the arXiv version/date stamp, its placement, and its associated self-link. Scientific content, experimental evidence, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility information remain identical throughout the main text and appendices, establishing no meaningful overall quality difference.
